message.content:
I don’t have live access to current air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment. In recent years LA’s air quality has improved compared to the 1990s, but it still often reaches “moderate” or even “unhealthy” levels on hot, dry days—especially during wildfire season when smoke from California fires can drift into the city.

If you want up‑to‑date information, check one of these reliable sources:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (EPA) | Search “Los Angeles” → see the latest AQI and pollutant breakdown. |
| **AQICN.org** | Global map; click on LA for real‑time readings. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish daily summaries and alerts. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., PurpleAir, AirVisual) | Provide real‑time sensor data and forecasts. |

These will give you the current AQI, the main pollutants (PM₂.₅, ozone, etc.), and health recommendations.
